To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
peripheral expansion of T regulatory cells (Treg), specific for an RNA-binding nuclear antigen, is mediated by plasmacytotic dendritic cells (DC) in a type 3 interferon (IFNs)-dependent manner.
plasmacytoidal dendritic cells (PDC) and type 1 IFNs promote peripheral expansion of La‐specific regulatory T (Treg) cells in a mouse model of La/Sjögern’s syndrome (SS) in vivo.
plasmacytotic dendritic cells promote the expansion of regulatory T cells specific to an RNA‐binding autoantigen in a type 2 interferon‐dependent manner.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular and cellular mechanisms of tolerance to self‐antigens, in particular, to nuclear antigens.
the role of plasmacytold dendritic cells in controlling autoreactive responses to RNA‐binding proteins.
how the body maintains tolerance to self‐antigens.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expansion of hLa‐Tg T cells expressing FoxP3 is mediated by pDC and type I IFNs.
pDCs and type 1 IFNs promote the accumulation of Foxp3+ Tregs specific for the RNA-binding nuclear antigen La in a mouse model of autoimmunity.
the accumulation of Foxp3+ Treg specific for the ubiquitous La/Sjögrens syndrome (SS)-B (La) RNA binding nuclear antigen is mediated through antigen presenting cells in an IFN-1 dependent manner.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the accumulation of Foxp3+ regulatory T cell (Treg) specific for a nuclear antigen, La, in mice expressing the antigen is dependent on the presence of plasmacytoldendritic cells (pDc) and type I interferons.
we have shown that the peripheral expansion of T cells that recognize a self‐antigen is regulated by pDC and type 1 IFNs.
plasmacytold dendritic cells are able to induce regulatory T cells in the context of an RNA‐binding antigen.
The main takeaway from our work is that

plasmacytold dendritic cells (PDCs) play a role in the induction and maintenance of regulatory T cells (CD4+CD25+FoxP3+ Treg) specific for RNA‐binding nuclear proteins, which are a major class self‐antigens that are targeted by autoreactive immune cells in autoimmune diseases, such as Sjögren's Syndrome (SS).
plasmacytold dendritic cells (a type of immune cell) can help to maintain immune tolerance to self‐antigens.

plasmacytold dendritic cells (PDC), which are known to be potent producers of type 1 interferons (IFN), play a critical role in promoting peripheral expansion of T cells specific for an RNA-binding nuclear antigen, La.
